Yes, you heard that right: the baby crying in this video is the lyrebird you see on screen. The imitation is so lifelike that it can feel a little unsettling, hence the warning.

Parrots are famous mimics, but the lyrebird, an Australian bird named for its tail, which looks like a lyre when fanned out, is even better. Besides a crying baby, it can copy the calls of other animals, car horns, the hiss of a steam train, an axe chopping wood, a rock crusher at a roadworks site and people shouting. It has even, mischievously, imitated the voice of Sir David Attenborough, the legendary narrator of BBC nature documentaries. Fanyu Meng calls it Australia’s little genius of mimicry.

Video: Guardian Australia, shared by Fanyu Meng on Ziyu Acoustics.
